recipes.name: Cheesy Ham and Hash Brown Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (32 ounce) package frozen hash brown potatoes
2 (10.5 ounce) cans condensed cream of potato soup

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.
Mix together hash browns, condensed soup, sour cream, Cheddar cheese, and ham in a bowl until well combined.
Spread evenly into the prepared dish. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly and lightly brown, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheesy Ham and Hash Brown Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This ham and hash brown casserole is a family-friendly dish made with hash brown potatoes and ham in a creamy sauce for a yummy, lazy day breakfast.

review.reviewBody: There are so many awesome reviews of this recipe that you may never even bother to read mine but . . . we have this at EVERY single family gathering. We have to plan the rest of the food around this recipe because the entire extended family insists upon this particular recipe. Others have brought different versions but they just don't cut it with the "fam." You cannot go wrong if you try this recipe. Don't subsitute cream of chicken or celery soup for the cream of potato. It's a key ingredient and worth the trip to the market to get it if you don't have it on hand.

I followed the recipe precisely, and this was yummy. I did cover loosely with foil after about 20 minutes when it looked like the edges were browning too early, but next time I'm just going to let it go. I didn't think a cup of ham would be enough or that this would actually serve 12, but it was just right. I used diced hash browns instead of the shreds, and shredded parmesan from a bag instead of the shaker can. Next time I might throw in some chopped jalapenos or green chiles for more zip -- bacon crumbles would be good too -- and the earlier reviewer's breakfast burrito idea for leftovers also sounds fabulous! This was super-easy to make up the night before. Thanks!

I made this for a church group and got rave reviews, and many recipe requests. I agreed with other reviewers that it was very salty, if you can use any low sodium ingredients do so. To the reviewer whose results were soupy, I wonder if you might have used ready to serve, rather than condensed soup. Thanks for sharing this recipe! 
This is an addition to my original review. I recently made this again, I omitted the Parmesan cheese, instead topping it with an additional handful of cheddar. This eliminated the salt problem! Wonderful stuff, try it you will be pleased!

For my son's First Holy Communion I had the whole family over for brunch after Church. Everyone raved about this recipe and I had to give the recipe to several people, I did make some changes that came out wonderful. I used 1 can of cheddar cheese soup and 1 can of potato soup, I also added bacon and used Oreda potatos O'brien, I can't tell you enough how easy and tasty this recipe is.

We love it! I've been making this for years and thus have tweeked it to our taste buds. I use 2 bags of simply potatoes Hashbrowns, one whole 8oz bag of Kraft Sharp Cheddar Cheese, one whole 24oz container of Daisy Sour cream, one whole 16oz bag of Great Value cooked ham cut in cubes, 3 cans of cream of potato, & one whole 6oz bag of Kraft parmesan cheese.

I added sautéed sweet peppers and onions. I also reduced the parmesan cheese topping to only one cup. I assembled it the night before and put in a cold oven. I left the foil over the casserole for 45 minutes then sprinkled the topping over it and cooked another 30 minutes.

My husband and I really liked this casserole but I did make some changes to it. I used pork sausage (mild) instead of ham, added a small onion, about 1/2 c. of sliced mushrooms, and half of a large green pepper. I sautéed the veggies in the same pan that I cooked the pork sausage. I used 2 cans of mushroom soup which seemed to go along with the fresh mushrooms. And, last, I used pepperjack cheese instead of cheddar and still put the Parmesan cheese on the top. I mixed it all up, except for the Parmesan, put it in a casserole dish, and cooked as directed. Still similar to the original recipe, just changed the protein, added some veggies (oh, I sprinkled some oregano and thyme on the veggies when I sautéed them), changed the flavor of soup and cheese. Now I have my version and the original recipe still to try. I am sure it is equally as good! We really liked this and went back for seconds.

I'm not sure about a breakfast casserole but I made this for a birthday dinner as a side dish. I use 1 can of cream of celery and 1 can of cream of mushroom and it was delicious! I covered this with tin foil until the last 3 minutes and then uncovered and turned on the broiler for the last 3 minutes to make the top a nice golden brown. It doesn't need any added salt but we all had to add black pepper. All and all excellent!

Hubby couldn’t stop raving about it. I added finely diced onion and seasoned pepper. I only had hash brown patties so I lined the pan with the patties, mixed the rest of the ingredients ( no Parmesan cheese so I added another cup of shredded cheddar) together and spread on top of the patties. Delicious! I did cut it in half and used an 11x7 pan

This was really yummy. I didn't have cream of potato soup so I used cream of mushroom (even though I’m not a fan of mushrooms). It was nice to make a meal without seasonings like salt. Everything together had a nice flavor. I made a smaller batch and used grated parm from a bag sprinkled on top with plain panko crumbs on top of that. Baked in my air fryer oven 360° for 45 mins.

We loved it! I made it for dinner to use up ham from my freezer. I added a lot more ham, 2 bags of frozen peas and thawed the hash browns. Combined those together and then added the liquid ingredients that were combined in a separate bowl. I only had 1 can of potato soup and 8 oz of sour cream so added 1 cup or so of milk. I made a second smaller casserole because it was overflowing my 9 x 13. It reheats well in the microwave. Came out delicious, moist and creamy not too cheesy. It's going into regular rotation for venison sausage instead of ham. I like that you can add any vegetable to customize the casserole.

Thanks for this recipe!
I have made this twice for a church fellowship dinner with zero leftovers. Quick and easy and very economical to prepare for a crowd.
This was awful but I know I'm in the minority. I almost didn't make based upon the ingredients and should not have wasted my time.
great for left over ham
The flavor was good, but the casserole was a little watery-more like potato soup than a casserole. I added pepper and Mrs. Dash for seasoning. I may cut back on the sour cream next tine.
My family absolutely loves this recipe! We make it several times a year, and love love it! 😋
I have made this recipe several times as is. All I have to say is that easier and tastier than this it is impossible!
We added peas for color and vegie.
Followed the directions. It was creamy and delicious. Everyone enjoyed it.
Switched ham for kielbasa and it's so good!
